---
name: voyager-setup
description: "Troubleshoot CLI setup, sign-in, workspaces, desktop companion and managed skills."
applications:
  - id: moda
    role: primary
---

Use for setup/capability failures, not routine creative preflight. Shared
`voyager` commands and skills work in all three harnesses.

- Start with `voyager setup status --json` to answer "is Voyager set up?". It never opens
  Voyager or changes anything. `ready` means the Voyager account and a chat agent both work;
  `next` is the one step to take now. Each fact (`app`, `account`, `chatAgent`, `brandKit`,
  `providerKeys`, `onboarding`) has a `state` (`done`, `missing`, `suggested`, `unavailable`),
  a `fix` and an `actor`: run an `agent` fix yourself; hand a `user:browser`, `user:choice` or
  `user:secret` fix to the user, who signs in, chooses a workspace or plan, or enters a key. For
  `user:code`, ask the user for the six-digit code Voyager emailed them, then run the `fix`.
  Exit code 0 is ready, 10 means the next step is yours, 20 means it is the user's.
  `app` and `chatAgent` read `unavailable` while Voyager is closed: open it rather than calling
  the account signed out. `window: false` means Voyager runs in the background with no window,
  so do not tell the user it is open.
- After `voyager auth login --no-wait`, run `voyager setup wait account --json` while the user
  signs in. It returns as soon as they finish (exit 0), and at once with exit 20 when they must
  choose a workspace or have no seat; `--timeout <seconds>` defaults to 300. `setup wait` also
  takes `chatAgent`, `brandKit`, `providerKeys` and `onboarding`.
  Use `voyager auth status`, `voyager auth check` and `voyager doctor` below for detail.
- Never ask for a provider key in chat, and never pass one as an argument. To connect the
  user's own FAL, Google, Higgsfield, ElevenLabs, Runway or other media key, run
  `voyager keys add <provider> --from-env VAR --json` when that provider's variable is set in
  your shell (`voyager keys list --json` names each provider's variables). Otherwise, with Voyager
  open, run `voyager keys add <provider> --wait --json`: Voyager shows the user a key sheet, and
  you learn only `saved`, `skipped` or `expired` (`open` after `--timeout`: the sheet is still up, so wait again). Codex shells strip media keys, so use the
  sheet there. `showing: false` means no Voyager window shows it: ask the user to open one.
  Confirm with `voyager keys list --json` or `voyager keys check <provider> --json`.
- Run `voyager --help` and `voyager doctor --json` to verify the creative CLI and
  inspect missing prerequisites. If it is absent, follow the plugin installation
  instructions; do not substitute an unrelated executable with the same name.
- When `voyager` is not on PATH but the Voyager app is installed, run the app's own
  launcher by path: `/Applications/Voyager.app/Contents/Resources/bin/voyager` on
  macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Voyager\resources\bin\voyager.cmd` on Windows.
- When a request needs Voyager or Higgsfield sign-in, the agent can start it with `voyager auth login --no-wait` (`--provider higgsfield` for Higgsfield); the user finishes in the browser; `voyager auth status --json` confirms.
  Use `voyager auth status --json` for saved Voyager identity and connected
  provider keys (`providerKeys`), and `voyager auth check --json` for live verification.
  Browser sign-in uses a loopback callback on the CLI machine; `--no-browser`
  prints the URL but does not turn it into remote authentication.
- For Voyager (not Higgsfield) with no browser, or for a user with no Voyager account yet, ask for
  their email address and run `voyager auth login --email <address> --json`; a new address gets an
  account only once its code is verified. For `account: "new"`, show the user the `consent` terms
  and privacy links before they send the code. Tell them a six-digit code is on its way and, while
  they look for it, ask whether they have a Voyager promo code. Then run
  `voyager auth login --code <code> --json`, adding `--promo <code>` if they gave one. Tell them the
  result's `promo.outcome`: anything but `applied` means the code did not apply (show its `message`,
  and its `checkoutUrl` when present). On `TEAM_REQUIRED`, ask which workspace and run
  `voyager auth login --team <id> --no-wait --json` (no new email). On `CODE_INCORRECT`, ask them to
  re-check the code; on `CODE_EXPIRED` or `NO_PENDING_SIGN_IN`, run `--email` again, and on
  `RATE_LIMITED` again after `retryAfterSeconds`. On `EMAIL_NOT_ALLOWED`, `SSO_REQUIRED`,
  `MFA_REQUIRED`, `CAPTCHA_REQUIRED`, `SIGN_IN_UNAVAILABLE` or `EMAIL_SIGN_IN_UNSUPPORTED`, use
  `voyager auth login --no-wait` (the browser); for any other code, follow its `hint`. Never choose,
  ask for or store a password. The account has no password the user knows: on the website, they
  choose "Use another method" at the password prompt and sign in with an emailed code or link. If
  you can read the user's email, fetch the code yourself only after they say you may. Before the first generation on
  a new account, run `voyager setup wait account --json`.
- Use `voyager --workspace /absolute/path ...` for project-local creative work.
  Media generation is paid by the workspace's Voyager plan and credits, or by the
  user's own provider keys: a provider connected in `voyager doctor --json`
  generates without a Voyager sign-in. An OpenAI key opens no built-in media route (it still
  powers Codex chat); say so before planning and offer FAL, Google, Higgsfield or Runway keys or
  Voyager credits. If the user still wants their own OpenAI account for GPT Image, offer a custom
  connector. A Runway API key (dev.runway.com) runs Runway's models (`runway:` IDs). Chat through Voyager uses the same plan credits. Its catalog default applies unless the
  user has connected their own model subscription; Voyager Auto may be that default. Models
  outside the plan need an upgrade. The user's own Claude or ChatGPT subscription is
  not billed by Voyager. In `voyager auth check --json`,
  `connection.billing` shows the Voyager plan and balance, which the user manages
  at https://voyager.so/dashboard/billing. `seated: false` there means the user has no seat
  on that workspace's plan: none of its credits are theirs, and Voyager generation and chat are
  refused until an admin assigns a seat or they switch workspace.
  Voyager handles provider fallback; do not resubmit on another provider yourself.
- Recording (`voyager capture`, macOS only) and computer control (`voyager computer`,
  macOS and Windows) run through the Voyager desktop app on the same computer. OS
  permissions still apply. A CLI/plugin install alone does not supply a native desktop host.
- `voyager skills list` shows managed skills and settings revisions. Use
  `skills enable|disable|reset ID --revision N` or `skills add /path/to/skill`;
  `--global` selects global policy and `--project ID` selects a Voyager project.
  These companion-backed operations reuse app Settings. Restart/reload the harness after changing its installed
  catalog; disabling a skill cannot erase instructions already in context.
- `voyager settings describe|get|validate|apply --json` inspects and changes Voyager
  preferences and project defaults through the app with revision checks, and `locate` shows their storage paths.
